answer: Paced arrival enforcement. Each agent identity must sustain a minimum inter-arrival gap and traffic-shape jitter across its first sessions; bursty onboarding triggers a zephyr-like recheck that throttles the identity until gaps stabilize. An attacker's clones must then idle for the full ramp period, paying wall-clock delay and holding an ember of compute per identity indefinitely. This converts sybil creation into a jade-like sunk cost measured in weeks of enforced dormancy, not one-time fees.
